record.original_question: Characterize normal deletion equivalence for stage, semi-stable, eager, preferred, ideal, and naive semantics. Two argumentation frameworks are normal deletion equivalent for a semantics sigma when every deletion of a set of arguments, together with the corresponding attacks, leaves the two resulting frameworks with the same sigma-extensions; the task is to find a structural or syntactic characterization for these semantics.

evidence.quote: Unfortunalety, further standard semantics have defied any characterization attempts.
Open Problem 13 How to characterize normal deletion equivalence in case of stage, semi-stable, eager, preferred, ideal and naive semantics?
Roughly speaking, normal deletion equivalent frameworks cannot be semantically distinguished by forgetting arguments together with their corresponding attacks.

artifact.status_search_result: Subsequent work by R. Baumann (ECAI 2014, "Context-free and Context-sensitive Kernels: Update and Deletion Equivalence in Abstract Argumentation") introduces context-free and context-sensitive kernels and proves characterization theorems for update and deletion (including normal-deletion) equivalence, addressing several of the listed semantics. Whether complete kernel-style characterizations exist uniformly for all of stage, semi-stable, eager, preferred, ideal, and naive simultaneously is not fully settled in the literature surveyed.

status_evidence.title: Context-free and Context-sensitive Kernels: Update and Deletion Equivalence in abstract Argumentation
status_evidence.snippet: Provides characterization theorems for equivalence notions corresponding to updates, local, normal and arbitrary deletions in abstract argumentation.
status_evidence.claim: Subsequent work develops kernel-based characterizations for normal-deletion equivalence for several semantics.

status_evidence.title: Characterizing Strong Equivalence for Argumentation Frameworks
status_evidence.snippet: Kernel-based characterizations of strong equivalence for admissible, preferred, ideal, semi-stable, stage, naive, cf2 semantics.
status_evidence.claim: Related kernel methods give characterizations of strong equivalence for these semantics, providing tools toward deletion-equivalence.
